## 2026-10-14 — Fail closed when platform reset status is unavailable

- **Reviewed:** Administrator platform-reset status polling, the reset preparation gate, backup/confirmation concurrency rules, and the existing reset-status client and server regressions.
- **Improvement:** Keep reset preparation disabled until a live status request succeeds, and disable it again when a refresh fails. A successful response clears the stale-status error and re-enables the action; the server-side reset gate and verified-backup workflow remain unchanged.
- **Why it helps:** An administrator cannot mistake an unavailable or stale status response for confirmation that no other reset is active. The destructive workflow now fails closed while preserving the existing retry and conflict-recovery message.
- **Backend review:** The server continues to serialize reset preparation, pause protected requests, require a verified backup, and reject competing reset attempts. No server change was needed.
- **Checked:** Added the dedicated `tests/client/platform-reset-status.test.js` regression; focused reset checks passed (8/8), the full `npm test -- --test-reporter=spec` suite passed (918/918), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` passed. ## 2026-10-14 — Reject impossible stored calendar deadlines

- **Reviewed:** The learner calendar's bounded date-range query, stored deadline normalization, malformed-date warning path, client month grouping, and existing invalid-deadline coverage.
- **Improvement:** Validate the calendar date portion before constructing a JavaScript `Date`, so impossible stored values such as `2099-02-31` are omitted and reported instead of being silently normalized into a different month.
- **Why it helps:** Learners no longer receive a deadline outside the requested calendar range with no warning when legacy or corrupted storage contains a rollover date; valid deadlines remain ordered and available.
- **Backend review:** The route still uses the existing bounded SQL range, access checks, summary batching, warning log, and additive `hasInvalidDeadlines` response flag. The change only tightens timestamp parsing before response serialization.
- **Checked:** Added a dedicated server regression covering an impossible February date alongside a valid deadline. The focused course-analytics suite passed (127/127); the full `npm test -- --test-reporter=spec` suite passed (917/917); `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` passed. The running app returned 200 from `/healthz`, `/readyz`, and the Vite root, and the connected in-app browser rendered `/register` with one heading and named controls. No credentials, forms, or application data were changed.

## 2026-10-12 — Retain quiz submission locks per route

- **Reviewed:** The learner quiz page's single in-flight route-key ref, route-change state resets, and the attempt endpoint's transactional insert. A pending submission on one quiz could be overwritten by a submission on another route, allowing a second attempt if the learner returned before the first finished; the route sequence also hid a successful response after returning to its quiz.

- **Backend review:** Attempt submission intentionally stores every valid retry in its existing immediate transaction; no server change was needed because the defect was loss of the client-side per-quiz in-flight lock.
- **Checked:** Focused keyed-request tests passed (4/4), full `npm test -- --test-reporter=dot`, `npm run build` (strict TypeScript checking and Vite), and `git diff --check` passed.

- **Improvement:** Build the editor payload inside the immediate transaction for both draft saves and publication. A short route comment explains that the payload read belongs before commit.
- **Why it helps:** A failed response read now rolls back the course, version, and audit changes together, so staff are not told a save failed after it took effect.
- **Checked:** The injected module-query failure reproduced the old draft-save behavior before the fix: HTTP 500 with the changed title and audit event committed. After the fix, draft and publication response-read failures roll back the course update, version, and audit event together. The full test suite and production build passed, including strict TypeScript checking; changed JavaScript files passed syntax checks, and `git diff --check` passed.

## 2026-10-11 — Keep platform settings response reads inside the write transaction

- **Reviewed:** The platform-settings PUT route committed setting changes and its audit entry before counting registered accounts and reading the response configuration. A failure in those follow-up reads returned an error after the change had already succeeded.
- **Improvement:** Build the complete response, including the registered-account count and effective settings, inside the immediate transaction. Response-read failures now roll back settings and the audit entry together.
- **Why it helps:** Administrators no longer receive a failed-save message for a setting change that was committed, and the returned account count describes the same transaction as the saved settings.
- **Checked:** A regression first reproduced the false failure: the route returned 500 while changing the platform name and palette. After the fix, the injected count-query failure returns 500 without changing either setting or adding an audit row. `node --test tests/server/registration-fields.test.js` passed (27/27); the full `npm test -- --test-reporter=tap` suite passed (494/494); `npm run build` passed strict TypeScript checking and Vite bundling; JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.

## 2026-10-11 — Keep the quiz pass threshold visible in results

- **Reviewed:** The new aggregate result panel showed the learner's correct-answer count and percentage but no longer displayed the quiz's pass mark. A learner who failed could not see what score they needed without returning to the quiz.
- **Improvement:** Show the score and pass threshold together. Failed results state the required percentage; passed results identify the threshold met. The existing quiz data already supplies the pass mark, so the result API stays aggregate-only.
- **Why it helps:** Learners can understand both their result and the target for a retry without exposing per-question answers or changing quiz scoring.
- **Checked:** Focused quiz result accessibility tests passed (4/4); the full `npm test -- --test-reporter=dot` suite passed; `npm run build` passed strict TypeScript checking and Vite bundling; `git diff --check` passed. Live result rendering was not exercised because it would require creating or changing a learner attempt.

## 2026-10-11 — Keep the current course version outside older-version pages

- **Reviewed:** The editor now keeps the latest published version visible and collapses older versions, but the API still counted that pinned version in the paginated list. At exactly 21 published versions, the first page therefore held only 19 of the 20 prior versions and exposed an unnecessary second page.
- **Improvement:** Return the current version separately, count and page only prior versions, and clamp requests using that prior-version count. Keep the current row visible even when a course has only one version, and show the exact number of older versions in the disclosure.
- **Why it helps:** The always-visible current version no longer consumes a history slot. Staff get complete 20-row pages and accurate counts while preserving bounded requests, indexed ordering, and restore actions for each older version.
- **Checked:** The course analytics route tests cover 42 versions over three pages, the exact 20-prior-version boundary, stale-page clamping, and the indexed query plan. The focused course-history/quiz tests passed (107/107); the full `npm test -- --test-reporter=dot` suite and `npm run build` (strict TypeScript plus Vite) passed. `git diff --check` passed. At 1999×1244 in the signed-in local browser, Version 8 remained visible, “Previous versions 7” started collapsed, and expanding it showed versions 7–1 with restore actions. No course data or publication controls were changed.

## 2026-10-11 — Close the session cleanup timer during shutdown

- **Reviewed:** The SQLite session store starts a daily expiry-pruning timer, while graceful shutdown drained HTTP requests and closed SQLite without explicitly stopping that timer. Several tests also reached into the store's timer property to clean it up.
- **Improvement:** Add an idempotent `close()` method, call it after the HTTP server drains and before closing SQLite, and use it in session-store test cleanup. Add a regression for repeated close calls.
- **Why it helps:** The store now has an explicit lifecycle boundary; its maintenance timer cannot run against a closed database, and tests no longer need to clear an internal timer directly.
- **Checked:** Focused session-store tests passed (8/8); `node --check` passed for the changed JavaScript files; `npm run build` passed; and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files. The first full-suite run had one 400-versus-201 failure in the uncommitted quiz-attempt regression; that file passed 2/2 in isolation and the repeated full suite passed. The quiz files were left untouched.

## 2026-10-11 — Review public course deadlines after path removal

My Learning is assembled from direct enrollments, grants, and published-path membership; Calendar reads saved deadline state and includes public courses that remain accessible after removal.

## 2026-10-11 — Keep profile updates atomic with certificate issuance

The administrator profile route already kept those writes in one transaction.

## 2026-10-11 — Explain account recovery when session storage fails

## 2026-10-11 — Stop media reads for already-closed responses

- **Reviewed:** Video and document routes check media with asynchronous `fs.stat` before creating a read stream. If a client disconnects while that check is pending, the response's `close` event has already fired when the stream helper installs its listener. A 16 MiB reproduction left the stream alive after reading 128 KiB.
- **Improvement:** Detect destroyed or already-ended responses before piping and destroy the new read stream immediately. Add a stream regression that verifies a pre-closed response causes zero file bytes to be read and no forwarded error.
- **Why it helps:** Learner navigation and disconnections during media lookup no longer leave a stalled file read or waste disk I/O for a response that cannot receive data.
- **Checked:** Focused stream tests passed (3/3); the pre-closed response reproduction now closes immediately with zero bytes read, no forwarded error, and no leftover close listener. The full `npm test -- --test-reporter=dot`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, syntax checks for both changed JavaScript files, and `git diff --check` passed.

## 2026-10-11 — Measure learner competency catalog response scaling

- **Reviewed:** The learner endpoint returns competency cards with their accessible mapped courses, and the page now renders those cards in batches while keeping an accurate full-map achievement summary.
- **Measurement:** In a temporary SQLite fixture, 1,000 active competencies each mapped to one completed public course distributed across five courses (200 mappings per course, within the editor limit) produced a 266,018-byte response. Catalogs of 50 and 250 produced 13,318 and 66,518 bytes. Each request prepared 10 SQL statements; median duration over five warmed loopback requests was 2.27 ms, 3.02 ms, and 6.88 ms respectively.
- **Result:** No API change. Response size scales linearly, but the tested 1,000-item case did not justify introducing a paged contract that would repeat the global progress calculation or require separate summary semantics. The client already bounds initial card rendering to 12 items.
- **Why no further change:** This synthetic single-process loopback fixture is not production latency or network evidence. Revisit backend payload paging if representative deployments show materially larger maps or slower transfer/processing.
- **Checked:** All benchmark data lived in a guarded temporary directory that was removed after the run; no repository or user database was used. The endpoint returned HTTP 200 for each size.

## 2026-10-11 — Preserve current learner filters after access changes

## 2026-10-11 — Cover expired-session cleanup failures

## 2026-10-11 — Reset watch checkpoints when replacing lesson video

- **Improvement:** Delete the lesson's watch-progress rows inside the media replacement transaction and include the number reset in the upload audit details. The telemetry rows cascade with watch progress; audit failure rolls the deletion back with the media update.
- **Why it helps:** The replacement starts from a clean watch checkpoint, and a failed upload audit preserves both the previous media and learner progress.

## 2026-10-11 — Resume tracked playback from verified progress after a tab is hidden

- **Interface review:** The account-details page already renders API error messages in its shared notice area, so the retryable limit response needs no new markup.

## 2026-10-10 — Invalidate in-flight CSRF refreshes across auth changes

- **Reviewed:** The API client’s shared CSRF refresh promise and the auth provider’s token clearing after sign-in, sign-up, setup, and sign-out.
- **Improvement:** Give CSRF state a generation. Clearing it now also detaches the in-flight refresh, and a response from an older generation waits for the current token instead of caching or returning its stale value. Add a deferred-response regression that failed before the change.
- **Why it helps:** Writes and retried uploads that overlap a session transition no longer receive a token from the previous session and spend their retry budget on a known-stale credential.
- **Interface review:** No rendered controls changed. Existing auth forms retain their current loading, error, and retry behavior.
- **Checked:** The new regression failed before the fix and passed afterward. Full `npm test` passed all 201 tests; `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, `node --check src/api.test.js`, and `git diff --check` passed.

## 2026-10-10 — Reject cancelled uploads while token refresh is pending

- **Reviewed:** Upload cancellation before XHR creation, the shared single-flight CSRF refresh, the multipart deferral added in the previous cycle, and cancellation during an upload retry.
- **Improvement:** Let each upload race its wait for a shared CSRF refresh against its own abort signal. Cancellation now rejects promptly without cancelling the shared refresh needed by other requests. Add a deferred-response regression that keeps the token request pending while verifying the upload has already rejected and created no multipart body or XHR.
- **Why it helps:** A stalled token endpoint can no longer keep a cancelled upload promise pending after its owning page has gone away.
- **Interface review:** Upload controls continue to use their existing abort signals; the change preserves shared token-refresh behavior and does not alter rendered controls.
- **Checked:** All 5 API-client tests passed; full `npm test` passed all 198 tests; `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, `node --check src/api.test.js`, and `git diff --check` passed.

## 2026-10-10 — Defer multipart creation until upload authorization is ready

- **Reviewed:** The upload helper after pre-cancel handling, the shared CSRF refresh’s asynchronous boundary, multipart construction, retry behavior, and the upload consumers’ abort signals.
- **Improvement:** Wait for the CSRF token and recheck cancellation before constructing the multipart body. Add a deferred-token regression proving that cancellation during token acquisition creates neither `FormData` nor an XHR.
- **Why it helps:** A page change or cancellation while session setup is pending no longer retains the selected file in a body that will never be sent.
- **Interface review:** Upload controls already abort when their owning view or request is replaced; no visual or markup change was needed.
- **Checked:** All 5 API-client tests passed; full `npm test` passed all 198 tests; `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, `node --check src/api.test.js`, and `git diff --check` passed.

## 2026-10-10 — Avoid repeated failed video-duration scans

## 2026-10-10 — Skip unchanged certificate-name submissions

- **Reviewed:** Account-detail form semantics and responsive layout, certificate-name normalization and certificate issuance, and the account update route's validation, no-op handling, session behavior, and audit writes.

## 2026-10-10 — Drive account course activity from user memberships

- **Reviewed:** The administrator account-details count and page queries, existing user-first enrollment/grant indexes, and the route's stable update/title ordering.
- **Improvement:** Build the account's course-ID set from enrollments and grants with `UNION`, then join those IDs to courses for the ordered page. The union keeps courses enrolled and granted to the same user from appearing twice.
- **Why it helps:** An account lookup can use the user's membership indexes and fetch only matching courses, instead of scanning the full course catalog and running membership checks for each course. The page still sorts the matched courses using the existing order.
- **Checked:** Before the change, SQLite scanned `courses` through its update-order index and evaluated two correlated membership checks per course. The new query-plan assertion confirms searches through `enrollments_user` and `grants_user`, then looks up matching courses by ID without scanning `courses`. The route test confirms overlap deduplication, the same total, and newest-first order. ## 2026-10-09 — Finish sign-out after session revocation

## 2026-10-09 — Return 404 for missing built assets

- **Reviewed:** Production static asset middleware, SPA deep-link fallback, current working-tree changes, and earlier tracker coverage for static asset caching.
- **Improvement:** Add an `/assets` miss handler after static serving so requests for missing built files return `404 text/plain` rather than falling through to the SPA HTML route.
- **Why it helps:** Browsers and proxies can recognize stale or invalid asset URLs as missing resources instead of treating the HTML app shell as a successful JavaScript or CSS response; valid assets and client-side routes keep their existing behavior.
- **Checked:** A production-mode server fixture confirmed a missing asset returns `404 text/plain`, a built JavaScript asset returns `200`, and `/courses/example` still returns the SPA HTML with `200`. `node --check server/index.js`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` passed.

## 2026-10-09 — Validate and publish courses atomically

- **Reviewed:** Course PATCH validation, publish-readiness checks, concurrent curriculum/media writes, no-op metadata updates, and audit ordering.
- **Improvement:** Re-read the course, validate its requested fields and publish readiness, and update its status within one immediate SQLite transaction; keep audit logging after commit.
- **Why it helps:** With multiple server processes sharing SQLite, a concurrent media or curriculum change can no longer slip between the readiness check and publication, leaving a published course incomplete.
- **Checked:** A two-worker Express/SQLite fixture confirmed a valid course publishes with `200`; while another connection held a write lock and removed the only lesson video, the waiting publish rechecked readiness and returned `400 course_incomplete`, leaving the course in draft. `node --check server/routes-courses.js`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` passed.

## 2026-10-09 — Match OpenDocument extensions to ZIP containers

- **Reviewed:** Lesson-document extension/MIME checks, ZIP and Compound File Binary (CFB) signature handling, and the earlier encrypted-OOXML compatibility decision.
- **Improvement:** Keep the CFB signature exception for encrypted `.docx`, `.pptx`, and `.xlsx` files, but require ZIP signatures for `.odt`, `.odp`, and `.ods` files.
- **Why it helps:** OpenDocument files with legacy Office bytes can no longer be stored under a misleading extension and then fail when a learner opens them; supported encrypted Office files remain accepted.
- **Checked:** An isolated Express/SQLite upload fixture rejected CFB uploads for all three OpenDocument types, accepted ZIP uploads for all six ZIP-based types, and retained CFB support for `.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`, `.doc`, `.ppt`, and `.xls`. The fixture confirmed only the 12 accepted resources were saved. `node --check server/routes-media.js`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` passed.

## 2026-10-09 — Avoid argument-limit failures when reordering large curricula

- **Reviewed:** Module and lesson reorder transactions, their unbounded sibling lists, and the temporary position calculation used before swapping unique positions.
- **Improvement:** Replace spread-based `Math.max(...items.map(...))` with a single-pass reduction for both modules and lessons.
- **Why it helps:** Reordering no longer throws a JavaScript `RangeError` when a large imported or accumulated curriculum exceeds the engine's function-argument limit; it also avoids allocating a second array of positions.
- **Checked:** The previous expression raised `RangeError` with 200,000 items; the new reduction returned the expected maximum for empty, ordinary, negative, and 200,000-item lists. `node --check server/routes-courses.js`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` passed.

## 2026-10-09 — Keep stale auth refreshes from restoring an old session

- **Reviewed:** The shared auth refresh used after self-access changes, the header and staff sign-out controls, and startup's overlapping StrictMode requests.

- **Why it helps:** A delayed refresh can no longer restore a user after a successful logout or overwrite a newer auth/settings state. Older overlapping startup refreshes also cannot publish stale results.

- **Checked:** An isolated transport harness confirmed a stale-token JSON write and multipart upload each refresh and succeed on one retry, ordinary server errors are not retried, and repeated CSRF rejection stops after two write attempts. `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` passed.

- **Reviewed:** `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` parsing, the example environment file, and the documented upload-size setting.
- **Improvement:** Require a positive safe whole-number byte count when the setting is supplied, and document that invalid values stop startup.
- **Why it helps:** Values such as `100MB`, decimals, or oversized integers can no longer be partially parsed or silently replaced by the 2 GB default, which could otherwise break uploads or exceed the operator's intended limit.
- **Checked:** Fresh Node processes accepted the default and valid byte counts and rejected unit suffixes, zero, negative, decimal, and unsafe-integer values. `node --check server/config.js`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` passed.

## 2026-10-09 — Validate the configured server port

- **Why it helps:** Malformed or out-of-range values no longer bind an unintended port or fail later with a lower-level server error.
- **Checked:** Fresh Node processes accepted the default and a valid custom port and rejected zero, negative, out-of-range, suffixed, decimal, and unsafe-integer values. `node --check server/config.js`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` passed.

## 2026-10-09 — Handle unsupported media ranges without a false 416

- **Improvement:** Return full `200` responses when range handling does not apply, including `HEAD`, `If-Range`, and unsupported or malformed range syntax. Keep `206` for supported single byte ranges and `416` for valid unsatisfiable byte ranges, following [RFC 9110 §14.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-14.2).
- **Why it helps:** Browsers that send multi-range or conditional requests no longer receive a misleading unsatisfiable response, while range seeking still works for supported requests.
- **Checked:** An isolated Express/SQLite fixture verified a single range, multi-range fallback, unknown unit, malformed range fallback, `If-Range` fallback, `HEAD` headers, and a genuinely unsatisfiable range. `node --check server/routes-media.js`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` passed.

- **Improvement:** Log a structured warning when removal of a session for a missing or disabled account fails, including the failure type and reason.
- **Why it helps:** Operators can see when invalid session rows are not being removed, while the affected request still proceeds as unauthenticated.
- **Checked:** An isolated temporary SQLite fixture forced deletion failures for both missing-user and disabled-user sessions; both warnings were recorded and both requests remained unauthenticated. Also checked `node --check server/http.js`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check`.

## 2026-10-09 — Validate stored password-hash encodings before scrypt

- **Reviewed:** The server's scrypt hash format, login and password-change bounds, and verification behavior for malformed SQLite values.
- **Improvement:** Require a bounded string, the exact supported scrypt parameters, the expected salt and digest lengths, valid hex, and exactly six encoded fields before invoking scrypt.
- **Why it helps:** Corrupt or unexpected stored values fail as invalid credentials without selecting unexpected scrypt settings or relying on permissive hex parsing.
- **Checked:** An isolated temporary fixture confirmed valid hashes still verify, wrong passwords fail, and unsupported parameters, malformed hex, extra fields, oversized values, and non-string values are rejected. Also checked `node --check server/auth.js`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check`.

## 2026-10-09 — Reduce login timing differences for unknown accounts

- **Reviewed:** Login lookup and password verification order, disabled-account behavior, stored-hash validation, the generic sign-in error, and the existing authentication rate limit.
- **Improvement:** Cache a random dummy scrypt hash and verify against it for missing, disabled, and malformed accounts; active accounts continue to verify against their stored hash.
- **Why it helps:** Allowed-length failed login attempts now perform comparable password-hashing work, reducing the response-time signal that can reveal whether a username belongs to an active account.
- **Checked:** An isolated temporary database fixture confirmed valid active credentials succeed while wrong, missing, disabled, and malformed accounts fail. Source inspection confirmed each allowed-length attempt verifies one supported scrypt hash. Also checked `node --check server/auth.js`, `node --check server/routes-auth.js`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check`.

## 2026-10-09 — Make large-upload request deadlines configurable

- **Improvement:** Add a validated `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` setting, defaulting to Node's existing five-minute timeout, and apply it to the HTTP server. Document the setting in `.env.example` and the configuration table.
- **Why it helps:** Self-hosters can extend the deadline for slower large uploads while keeping a nonzero timeout to protect the service from stalled request bodies.
- **Checked:** Config validation accepted the default and a custom value, rejected zero, non-integers, and values above the supported timer range, and a Node HTTP server accepted the configured timeout. Also checked `node --check server/config.js`, `node --check server/index.js`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check`.

## 2026-10-09 — Reject non-text course content

## 2026-10-12 — Recheck learner quiz-result recovery and access

- **Reviewed:** Quiz result semantics, saved-score fallback when answer details fail, retry behavior, focus after submission, course payload trimming, and the attempt-detail API's learner and course scoping.
- **Result:** No code change. The attempt endpoint verifies course access and selects by attempt ID, quiz ID, and current learner ID. The client keeps the saved aggregate score visible when the question breakdown is unavailable and only retries transient detail failures.

- **Checked:** Focused quiz-result UI and API tests passed (13/13), including malformed stored snapshots, learner scoping, trimmed payloads, and accessible retry/status feedback. `git diff --check` passed.

## 2026-10-12 — Recheck request failures and server shutdown

- **Reviewed:** The shared API client's network, abort, malformed-response, CSRF-retry, and upload-timeout handling; server request-timeout configuration, structured HTTP errors, and graceful shutdown.
- **Result:** No runtime change. The client preserves aborts, distinguishes connection loss from invalid JSON, limits CSRF retries, and explains uncertain upload completion. The server returns structured body and upload errors, stops accepting connections on shutdown, and closes active connections after the grace period before closing the session store and database.
- **Why no change:** Existing behavior covers the reviewed failure paths without a reproduced stalled request, misleading error, unsafe retry, or shutdown leak.
- **Backend review:** The default request timeout is five minutes and is configurable within Node's timer range; shutdown has a 30-second drain deadline. No missing server behavior surfaced in the inspected paths.
- **Checked:** `node --test tests/client/api.test.js tests/server/config.test.js` passed (25/25); `node --test tests/server/last-login.test.js tests/server/media-routes.test.js` passed (43/43), including structured request errors and interrupted uploads. `git diff --check` passed.
- **Needed to continue:** A reproducible request that stays pending or reports the wrong recovery action, an unsafe duplicate after retry, or a shutdown trace showing open resources after the grace period.

## 2026-10-12 — Recheck learner course catalog filters and paging

- **Reviewed:** Catalog search and filter state, request cancellation and sequence guards, page-drift recovery, empty/loading/error announcements, responsive filter and card-grid rules, and the learner catalog API's validation, access filters, stable ordering, and bounded pagination.
- **Result:** No runtime change. Filter changes apply the visible search draft and restart at page one; additional pages deduplicate IDs and refresh when totals, ordering, or page boundaries drift. The API applies the same role-aware visibility rules to results and category options.
- **Why no change:** The client and server contracts align, and the reviewed empty, retry, cancellation, access, and pagination paths already have regression coverage. No current-build visual mismatch or data-backed performance issue was found.
- **Backend review:** Search, category, sort, and page inputs are validated; regular learners only receive public or explicitly granted courses, while staff may browse private courses. Result pages use bounded limits and deterministic tie-break ordering.
- **Checked:** `node --test tests/client/course-catalog-filters.test.js tests/client/course-pagination-announcements.test.js tests/server/course-analytics.test.js` passed (134/134); `git diff --check` passed.
- **Needed to continue:** A reproducible current-build catalog mismatch, an inaccessible filter or paging interaction, or representative catalog size/latency data showing a specific query bottleneck. Rendered responsive catalog behavior was not rechecked in this cycle.

## 2026-10-12 — Keep accessible names on empty image previews

- **Reviewed:** The shared `ImageWithFallback` component and its branding and course-cover call sites. A failed image URL retained meaningful `alt` text, but a valid empty `src` rendered only the visual placeholder.
- **Improvement:** Reuse one fallback renderer for missing sources and failed loads. It keeps non-empty image alternatives in the accessibility tree while leaving decorative `alt=""` fallbacks unnamed.
- **Why it helps:** New course drafts and platforms without a custom icon now expose the same useful preview name before an image is uploaded, while the visible placeholder stays unchanged.
- **Backend review:** Branding responses intentionally return `platformIcon: null` when no icon is configured, and course editor payloads return `coverUrl: null` when no cover exists. The settings API already supports icon removal; no backend change was needed.
- **Checked:** The focused regression failed before the fix because the no-source branch discarded `alt`. The signed-in local course editor rendered a draft with no cover; the accessibility tree exposed “Course cover preview” through the visually hidden image name while the BookOpen placeholder remained visible. No console warnings or errors appeared. `npm test -- --test-reporter=dot` passed (834/834), `npm run build` passed strict TypeScript checking and Vite, and `git diff --check` passed.

## 2026-10-12 — Explain empty published course content

- **Reviewed:** The learner course overview's empty curriculum behavior, both “Start learning” actions, activity navigation, and the backend rule that validates course content before publication.
- **Improvement:** Show a semantic “No learning activities yet” empty state when a published record has no lessons or quizzes. Hide the inert start actions unless a next activity exists, while preserving certificate and progress actions for completed or in-progress records.

Focused course navigation and overview checks passed (16/16), the full Node test suite passed, and `npm run build` passed strict TypeScript checking and Vite bundling. `git diff --check` passed. Rendered empty-state QA was not run because the repository has no Playwright dependency and no empty-course browser fixture was created in the development database.

## 2026-10-12 — Keep calendar overflow inside its panel

- **Reviewed:** The learner calendar grid at 320px, its 640px minimum readable width, the panel's horizontal scrolling, and document-level scroll metrics across key learner and staff routes.
- **Improvement:** Clip horizontal overflow at the document root while preserving the calendar panel's own scroll container. Include a hidden-overflow fallback for older browsers.
- **Why it helps:** Narrow learners no longer get a second page-level horizontal scrollbar for the calendar. The full month remains reachable through the focused calendar panel and its existing scroll cue.
- **Backend review:** The calendar endpoint already bounds the requested month range, validates dates, and returns only accessible deadlines; no server change was indicated.
- **Checked:** At 320px before the fix, the calendar rendered `documentElement.scrollWidth` wider than the viewport while `.calendar-panel` already had its own scroll width. The focused calendar/responsive checks passed (7/7), the full `npm test` suite passed (854/854), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` passed. The signed-in local browser at 320 × 720 showed the calendar panel still scrollable without a second page-level horizontal scrollbar; Previous month changed October 2026 to September 2026 and This month restored October 2026. No console warnings or errors appeared.
